_note: Purpose catalogue for v2 classification. The user picks the intended purpose; EU AI Act Annex III classification is derived from this, never from technology. Annex refs follow Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Annex III as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. See docs/v2/classification-spec.md.

purposes.label: Identify people at a distance from biometric data (e.g. face matching against a watchlist)
examples: Facial recognition of shoppers against a banned-persons list
Matching CCTV footage against a database of faces
purposes.notes: Excludes biometric verification whose sole purpose is to confirm a person is who they claim to be (see biometric_verification). Real-time use in public spaces for law enforcement is screened under Art. 5(1)(h).

purposes.label: Confirm a person is who they claim to be (1:1 biometric check)
purposes.notes: Expressly excluded from Annex III 1(a). Biometric data still raises the governance tier.

purposes.label: Sort people into categories from biometric data (e.g. age, gender, sensitive traits)
examples: Estimating age band from a face image
purposes.notes: Annex III 1(b) covers categorisation by sensitive or protected attributes. Inferring race, political opinions, trade union membership, religion, sex life or sexual orientation is prohibited under Art. 5(1)(g).

purposes.label: Infer people's emotions or intentions from biometric data (face, voice, physiology)
purposes.notes: Prohibited in the workplace and in education except for medical or safety reasons (Art. 5(1)(f)). Physical states such as pain or fatigue are not emotions (Recital 18).

purposes.label: Safety component in operating critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or water, gas, heating or electricity supply
examples: AI controlling pressure safety in a water network
AI safety layer in traffic-signal control
purposes.notes: No FRIA (Art. 27), no Art. 86 explanation right, and no Art. 49(3) public-deployer registration for point 2.

purposes.label: Decide admission to, or assignment within, an education or training institution
Evaluate learning outcomes (grading, assessment, steering learning)
examples: Adaptive tutoring that grades and routes students

purposes.label: Assess what level of education a person should receive or can access
examples: Placement testing that sets a student's track

purposes.label: Monitor or detect prohibited behaviour of students during tests
Recruit or select people: targeted job ads, filtering applications, evaluating candidates
examples: Targeting job adverts to selected audiences
purposes.notes: Drafting job-ad text with no targeting or candidate evaluation is not this purpose (use internal_productivity_assistant).

purposes.label: Decide on promotion, termination or terms of work; allocate tasks by behaviour or traits; monitor or evaluate workers
examples: Gig-platform task allocation based on driver behaviour

purposes.label: Evaluate eligibility for public assistance benefits or services, or grant, reduce, revoke or reclaim them
purposes.notes: Only high-risk when used by, or on behalf of, a public authority.

purposes.label: Evaluate the creditworthiness of individuals or set their credit score
purposes.notes: Fraud detection is expressly carved out (use fraud_detection). Covers natural persons only.

purposes.label: Assess risk or set prices for individuals' life or health insurance
purposes.notes: Other insurance lines (motor, home) are not Annex III 5(c).

purposes.label: Assess risk or set prices for individuals in other insurance or contracts (not life/health insurance, not credit)
purposes.notes: Not Annex III: 5(c) covers only life and health insurance. Profiling still raises the tier.

purposes.label: Classify emergency calls, dispatch or prioritise emergency services, or triage emergency patients
Law-enforcement use: victim risk, polygraph-type tools, evidence reliability, (re)offending risk, profiling in investigations
examples: Risk of re-offending assessment supporting a human
purposes.notes: Predicting offending based solely on profiling or personality traits is prohibited (Art. 5(1)(d)).

purposes.label: Migration, asylum or border control: risk assessment, application examination, identification
purposes.notes: Verification of travel documents is excluded from 7(d).

purposes.label: Assist a court or dispute-resolution body in researching or interpreting facts and law, or applying law to facts
examples: Judicial research assistant used by a court

purposes.label: Influence the outcome of an election or referendum, or how people vote
purposes.notes: Excludes tools whose outputs people are not directly exposed to, e.g. campaign logistics.

purposes.label: Detect fraud or financial crime
purposes.notes: Expressly carved out of Annex III 5(b).

purposes.label: Answer customer questions or handle service requests
Help staff draft, summarise, search or analyse (general productivity)
Generate text or media for marketing, communications or publishing
Provide a tool that generates or edits images, video, audio or voices
purposes.notes: Screened against the 2026 prohibitions on non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM.

purposes.label: Write, review or test software code
Extract, classify or route documents and data
Automate business tasks or workflows, including agents acting through tools
examples: Procurement agent that raises and pays purchase orders

purposes.label: Recommend or personalise products, content or offers
Profile or segment people for marketing (not employment, credit or elections)
Forecast or optimise operations (demand, logistics, pricing of goods)
Detect security threats or anomalies in systems
Support diagnosis, treatment or clinical decisions
purposes.notes: High-risk via Annex I if the software is a medical device needing notified-body conformity assessment (MDR/IVDR).

purposes.label: Part of a regulated physical product (machinery, toys, lifts, vehicles, radio equipment, etc.)
examples: Visual quality inspection on a production line
purposes.notes: Since Reg. (EU) 2026/1744, 'safety component' is limited to functions that prevent or mitigate health and safety risks. Pure optimisation does not qualify.

purposes.label: Develop or release a general-purpose AI model (not a specific application)
examples: Training and publishing a foundation model
Releasing a substantially fine-tuned base model

purposes.label: Something else
purposes.notes: All prohibited-practice screens are shown. Consider whether any Annex III purpose applies.
